newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PX50 CLOSES DOWN DESPITE MAY TRADE DATA.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PX50 CLOSES DOWN DESPITE MAY TRADE DATA.

text.p: 1400 GMT - Czech PX50 index falls sharply on Monday despite
May trade figures widely welcomed as positive by economists.
* PX50 closes down 8.1 points, 1.6 percent, to 498.3
Czech shares took a beating on Monday despite the release of better than expected foreign trade figures showing the May trade deficit at 11.2 billion crowns down from 15.4 billion in April.
Despite the news, equity dealers said it would probably take several more months of positive data before foreign investors would be persuded to return to the Czech market.
"In the second half of this year, all the important indicators should slightly improve compared to the first half and this should help the markets overall," said Radim Bajgar of ING Barings.

On Monday, Bajgar said that the PX50 index, which fell 1.6 percent to 498.3, had probably been hit by a combination of profit talking in SPT Telecom and fundamental worries about the cost of some of power utility CEZ's long term investments. He specifically mentioned concerns at the rising cost of completing the Temelin nuclear power plant.
SPT Telecom dropped 40 crowns to 3,375 and CEZ fell 27 crowns to 900.
Komercni Banka lost 112 crowns to 1,795 and Ceska Sporitelna was down six crowns to 293.
